title: the autopilot reloads merged code by itself: it drains its running jobs and its old code hands off to a fresh snapshot, never killed; the board only says, in English and Chinese, when it runs older code
acceptance: Why. A merged change to the autopilot never takes effect until someone kills the running service by hand. `bin/fm-autopilot.sh` mode `ensure` exits 0 as soon as `python3 "$HERE/lib/fm_autopilot.py" running` sees `service.lock` held (bin/fm-autopilot.sh:52-54, `live()` at bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:766-772), and `serve` records only `pid`, `owner` and `started` in `state/autopilot/owner.json` (:800), so nothing can tell that the engine checkout has moved on. On 2026-10-05 the autopilot ran pre-T-190 code for hours after T-190 merged (state.json had no `poll_seq`, no `migrated_t190`); firstmate restarted it by hand after T-193, T-200 and T-199. The board has a similar gap (`board_start`, bin/fm-herdr.py:2340-2380, reuses any verified board and bun loads board/server.ts once, so T-192, T-198 and T-202 each needed a manual restart); this task only makes that visible with a notice. Automatic board replacement is a separate follow-up task, not part of T-203. Killing is not safe for the autopilot: every gate, protocol and review job is a child owned by the serve pid (`life.start(..., owner=os.getpid())`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:278), so a kill ends them all, and `recover_jobs` (fm_autopilot_loop.py:303-310) then marks each `uncertain` and queues a reconciliation wake.

Which code. The code source is the engine checkout, `ctx['engine']` (FM_ENGINE_ROOT, which `fm_storage_init` sets to the `--repo` root, bin/fm-config.sh:941-945). Add `code_id(path, folders)` to bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py as a module-level function near `live`: it first checks that `<path>/.git` exists (a directory or a gitfile) without starting any process, and returns None when it does not; otherwise it runs `git -C <path> rev-parse --show-toplevel HEAD:<folder>...` (one call: the top level, then one tree id per folder) and `git --no-optional-locks -C <path> status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <folders>`; both calls run with `--no-optional-locks` (and the environment GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0) (and in the board notice's copy below), so a `git status` never takes `.git/index.lock` and firstmate's `git merge --ff-only` in the same checkout can never fail on it (gitignored files such as `__pycache__/` do not count), and returns `dict(<folder>=<tree id>..., dirty=<bool>)`, or None when `git -C <path> rev-parse --show-toplevel` does not resolve to <path> itself (not a repository, or a folder inside another checkout) or any command fails. Comparison rule, used everywhere a code id is compared (`running`, `reload_due`, `handoff_target`, the board notice): two ids are equal only when every tree id matches and neither has `dirty: true`; a recorded dirty id is different from every id, including a clean one with the same tree ids, so a service started from uncommitted edits reloads to the committed code once the tree is clean. Ignored files never count: the dirty check is `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`, which honours the checkout's .gitignore (the repository's .gitignore already ignores `__pycache__/`, :9); bytecode written by running the code therefore never makes it dirty. The autopilot uses folders `bin` and `skills`. The short form in messages is `<first 7 of each tree id joined by />`, plus `+dirty` when dirty, or `unknown` for a record without code. Two git processes per project are the whole cost (one rev-parse, one status); nothing is hashed, because `ensure --resume --all` runs this for each registered project on every operator `fm` command (bin/fm.sh:993-1005). `fm_freeze` snapshots the tree that owns the invoked entrypoint (bin/fm-herdr.py:2412-2419), which in production is the engine checkout; every handoff below invokes `<ctx['engine']>/bin/fm-autopilot.sh` with FM_CODE_ROOT, FM_ENTRY_PID and FM_ENTRY_SCRIPT removed from its environment, so the new snapshot is taken from the engine checkout and matches the code id it is compared with.

reload.json. `state/autopilot/reload.json` has fixed fields and is only ever updated by read-modify-write under `start.lock` (the existing `Locked(directory / 'start.lock')`), by every writer (`running`, `serve`, the old service during handoff); no writer replaces it wholesale. Fields: `request` = `{to, from, requested}` or null (the pending reload); `outcome` = `{kind: 'reloaded'|'failed', from, to, at, error, reported, woken}` or null (the last outcome only); `failed_ids` = list of code ids whose handoff failed (never retried); `dirty_seen` (last dirty id reported); `legacy_seen` (last pre-change service pid reported).

The service records its code. `ensure` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:774-789) computes `code_id(ctx['engine'], ('bin','skills'))` before it starts `serve` and passes it as JSON in the child environment variable `FM_AUTOPILOT_CODE` (unset when None), and the temporary owner.json it writes before starting the child (:779, `pid: None`) also carries `code` (the id or null); `serve` always writes the field `code` into owner.json: the id object, or JSON `null` when FM_AUTOPILOT_CODE is unset (code_id returned None). Reading rule: a missing `code` field means a service started before T-203; `code: null` means a post-T-203 service whose code is unknown and counts as different from any real id (it reloads once a real clean id exists). `serve` writes plus `snapshot` = its FM_CODE_ROOT (the frozen `state/snapshots/code-*` directory it runs from), beside `pid`, `owner` and `started`. The window in which HEAD could move between `fm_freeze` and `code_id` is accepted and stated in docs: the next `ensure` sees the difference and reloads.

Reload request, never a kill. `fm_autopilot.py running` keeps its exit contract (0 = a service holds service.lock, 1 = none), so bin/fm-autopilot.sh:52-54 stays one call; when it exits 0 it also compares current = `code_id(ctx['engine'], ('bin','skills'))` with owner.json `code`, under `start.lock`. First, an owner.json with `pid: None` (ensure's temporary record) or without `started_ok: true` is a service still starting: nothing is requested, cleared or printed, so a reload in progress keeps its `request` until the new serve records its outcome. (a) current is None, or current equals owner.json `code` by the comparison rule (a recorded dirty id never equals a clean current id): nothing is requested, and a `request` already recorded is cleared (the checkout went back to what runs). (b) current is dirty: nothing is requested, a `request` already recorded is cleared, and stderr gets `fm-autopilot: bin/ or skills/ has uncommitted changes; keeping the running code <old>` once per distinct current id (remembered as `dirty_seen`). (c) owner.json has no `code` field at all (`code: null` is not this case; it falls under (d) as a different id): the running service predates this change and its loop cannot act on a request, so nothing is requested; stderr gets `fm-autopilot: the running service predates self-reload (T-203); restart it by hand once, when no job is running` once per service pid (remembered as `legacy_seen`). (d) owner.json `code` is null or a different id, current is clean, and the id is not in reload.json `failed_ids`: set reload.json `request` = `{to: <current>, from: <owner code>, requested: <time>}` (only when `request.to` is not already the same id), ring the service with `life.ring_events(ctx['state'], 'autopilot reload requested')` (bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py:531) and print `fm-autopilot: reload requested: <old>-><new>; it restarts when its running jobs finish`. A request already recorded for the same `to` prints nothing. No signal is ever sent to the service. Also in `running`, only when it exits 0 (a live service) and the environment variable FM_AUTOPILOT_HANDOFF is not set (the old service sets FM_AUTOPILOT_HANDOFF=1 for its handoff child, whose output goes to service.log): when reload.json `outcome` is not yet `reported`, print `fm-autopilot: reloaded: <old>-><new>` or `fm-autopilot: reload to <new> failed (<error>); running the previous code <old>; inspect service.log` once and set `reported: true`. That is how the outcome reaches the operator: on the next `fm` command or `fm-session.sh start` (both pass ensure's stderr through, bin/fm.sh:1004, bin/fm-session.sh:99); `fm-autopilot.sh status` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:822-824) adds a `reload` key holding reload.json's `request`, `outcome` and `failed_ids` to its JSON.

Idle check. A module-level `reload_due(pilot, own_code, reload)` returns true only when `reload['request']` is set, its `to` is not equal to `own_code` by the comparison rule (so a service running a dirty snapshot reloads to a clean `to` with the same tree ids), its `to` is not in `failed_ids`, and the service is idle: no `pilot.data['jobs']` entry in state `running` or `consuming`, no `pilot.data['actions']` entry in state `started`, `pilot.data['batches']` empty, and every `pilot.data['wakes']` entry `pushed`. Jobs in `uncertain` or `done` do not block. While not idle the service keeps working normally.

Handoff, run by the old code. In `serve`'s loop (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:808-814), after `pilot.flush()`, when `reload_due` is true the service calls a module-level `handoff_target(ctx, own_code, reload)`, which computes `code_id(ctx['engine'], ('bin','skills'))` again and returns None if it is None, dirty, or equal to `own_code` by the comparison rule, and that id otherwise. On None the service clears `request` under start.lock and stays in the loop (no handoff, nothing recorded); otherwise it sets `request.to` to the returned id under start.lock and leaves the loop, so `with` releases service.lock and closes its doorbell. Still running its own (old) code, it then runs `<ctx['engine']>/bin/fm-autopilot.sh ensure --repo <ctx['engine']>` (plus `--project <ctx['project']>` when ctx names one) as a child through `life.start(..., owner=<its own session owner from life.session_owner()>)` with the environment described above, FM_SESSION_PID set to that same owner and FM_AUTOPILOT_HANDOFF=1, stdin closed and stdout/stderr appended to service.log. Lock probes never fool each other or turn a service away: `live()` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:766-772) probes with a shared lock, `LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB`, released at once; shared probes never block one another, so `running` (bin/fm-autopilot.sh:53) and `ensure`'s `if live(directory): return` (:778) report a service only when a `serve` holds the exclusive lock, never because another probe was in flight. A probe can still collide with a `serve` taking `LOCK_EX`, so and `serve` (:797-798) no longer returns 0 on the first `BlockingIOError`: it retries `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` every 100 ms for up to 2 s and returns 0 only if the lock is still held after that, so a concurrent `running` check, the old service's success poll or a test's probe can no longer turn away the new service or the re-executed old one, while a genuine second service still gives up. Every `serve` (new or old code) writes owner.json as today plus `code`, `snapshot` and, once `pilot.recover()` and `pilot.recover_jobs()` have returned (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:803-804), `started_ok: true`. The new serve, at that same point and under start.lock, if reload.json `request` is set and its own code differs from `request.from`, sets `outcome` = `{kind: 'reloaded', from: request.from, to: <its own code>, at}` and clears `request`; its own code is what it actually runs, which may be newer than `request.to` if HEAD moved in between. The old service does not probe service.lock while that child runs; it waits for the child to exit (bounded by the same wait) and only then checks. Success, as seen by the old service: within `FM_AUTOPILOT_RELOAD_WAIT` seconds (default 60; tests set a few seconds), a live service.lock holder whose owner.json has a pid other than the old service's, `started_ok: true`, and a `code` different from the old service's own. Then the old service exits 0. Before recording a failure the old service re-reads owner.json under start.lock: if a live service.lock holder by then has `started_ok` and a code different from its own, that is success after all. If a live holder with a different pid exists but has not yet set `started_ok` (a slow start), it is success pending: the old service keeps waiting up to a second `FM_AUTOPILOT_RELOAD_WAIT` bound, and if the holder is still alive with a code different from its own at the end, the old service records nothing as failed, exits 0, and leaves `request` for the new serve, which records `reloaded` when its start-up finishes. The old service never records `failed`, adds to `failed_ids` or queues the failure wake while a live holder with a different code exists; only when no other live holder exists (or it runs the old code) is the handoff a failure. Otherwise (the child exited non-zero, the new code could not import, the new service died before or after `ready`, or the wait passed) the old service, under start.lock, sets `outcome` = `{kind: 'failed', from: <own code>, to: request.to, at, error}` (error = the last non-empty line the child wrote to service.log, or `no new service within <n> s`), appends `request.to` to `failed_ids`, clears `request`, and restarts itself with `os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, <its own fm_autopilot.py>, 'serve'])` and its unchanged environment (FM_AUTOPILOT_OWNED=1 and the old FM_AUTOPILOT_CODE), so the previous code keeps serving. Between leaving the loop and the re-executed serve taking service.lock nobody holds the lock; an `fm` command in that window runs `ensure`, which may start a service itself (from the current checkout, under start.lock, exactly as today for a missing service); service.lock still guarantees one holder, the re-executed old serve then finds the lock held and returns 0, and whichever service holds the lock is the one that runs. That re-executed serve finds `request` cleared and its own code equal to `outcome.from`, so it writes no `reloaded`. If another service holds service.lock by then, that serve returns 0 as today and the live service stays. Wake: after a serve has taken service.lock and run recover/recover_jobs, if `outcome.kind` is `failed` and not `woken`, it queues one firstmate wake through `pilot.queue('reload-failed-' + <short form of outcome.to>, '', 'Autopilot reload to <new> failed; running the previous code <old>; inspect service.log', '自動駕駛重載到 <new> 失敗；仍執行先前的程式 <old>；請檢查 service.log')` and sets `woken: true` under start.lock; only the lock holder queues it. A failed id is never retried (`failed_ids`); only a different clean id is requested. The service's recovery never depends on the new code. A request is only ever written by `fm_autopilot.py running` of the copy that runs bin/fm-autopilot.sh (the engine checkout when called from bin/fm.sh:1004; the session's frozen snapshot when called from bin/fm-session.sh:99, taken from the engine checkout moments earlier), always comparing against `code_id(ctx['engine'])`. From bin/fm.sh, so a commit whose bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py cannot import never produces a request: `running` fails, bin/fm-autopilot.sh falls through to `fm_freeze` and the new snapshot's `ensure`, which fails too, so every `fm` command prints today's `fm: autopilot unavailable; inspect project state/autopilot/service.log` (bin/fm.sh:1004-1005) and takes one fresh snapshot (bin/fm-herdr.py:595-610), while the old service keeps serving and holding service.lock. That is accepted and stated in docs; the `unavailable` line is what tells firstmate. `Pilot`'s class body, the migration block (:66-108) and every restack, recheck or advance function are not edited (the migration block and restack code changed with T-204, which has merged).

Board: a notice only, never a restart. `board_start` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2340-2380) records in state/session/board.json `code` = the tree ids of HEAD:board and HEAD:i18n plus `dirty`, computed by a new `board_code_id(root)` in bin/fm-herdr.py with the same rules as `code_id` (the `.git` check first, without starting a process; `--no-optional-locks` on both git calls; None when <root> is not the top level of a git work tree), on a fresh start; on reuse it copies the previous board.json's `code` forward unchanged (board.json is rewritten on every call, :2376-2379). On reuse it also compares that recorded code with the current `board_code_id(root)` by the comparison rule. When both exist and differ, the returned record and board.json carry `stale: true` and `stale_reason` = `{en: 'the board runs older code (<old> -> <new>); restart it by hand: stop the board process and run fm board', 'zh-TW': '看板仍在執行較舊的程式（<old> -> <new>）；請手動重啟：停止看板程序後執行 fm board'}`; `fm board` prints the English and the zh-TW line on stderr as two `fm board:` lines and keeps today's exit status (0, or 69 for `sign_in_error`, :2738-2739); `fm-session.sh start`'s JSON report carries it as `board.stale_reason` (the session prints `board_start`'s record, :2809-2810). `stale`/`stale_reason` describe only the current call: when the current code is None or dirty, board.json is missing, or it has no `code` (a board started before this change, whose code is unknown), or the codes are equal, neither field is written and nothing is printed. The board is never stopped, signalled or replaced by this task. Automatic replacement, which must first make running merges, dispatches and send-back answers safe, is a separate follow-up task.

Who moves the engine checkout. Unchanged: after a merge, firstmate fast-forwards the engine checkout (`git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` in the engine root); this task does not pull or fetch. The next `ensure` (every `fm` command, or `fm-session.sh start`) sees the new tree ids and acts as above, and the next `fm board`/session start prints the board notice when it applies. The running autopilot predates this change and its old code cannot act on any of this: after this merges, firstmate restarts it by hand once, when no job is `running` or `consuming` in state.json, by the kill-and-ensure procedure used today; from then on it reloads itself. The board still needs a manual restart whenever its code changes; the notice says when.

Tests (workers do not run them; evidence is the required check and the gates). (1) New tests/lib/autopilot_reload.py with tests/autopilot-reload.test.sh, beside tests/lib/autopilot_lifecycle.py and using its owner-process pattern: the temporary root is `git init`-ed with bin/, skills/, config.yaml and .gitignore copied from the checkout and committed (the copied .gitignore is what keeps `bin/lib/__pycache__/` from making the fixture dirty), the test asserts `code_id` reports the fixture clean right after the first ensure, FM_CODE_ROOT is not set, and the fixture's own bin/fm-autopilot.sh is invoked, so the snapshot and the code id come from the same tree. (a) ensure starts a service whose owner.json `code` equals the fixture's tree ids; ensure again keeps the pid and prints nothing. (b) Commit a change under bin/ (a comment line in bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py), run ensure: stderr has `reload requested`; the service drains (no jobs), hands off, and a new pid holds service.lock with the new `code`; the old pid has exited (ProcessExit) and at no point do two processes hold service.lock; the next ensure prints `reloaded:` once and then nothing. (c) An uncommitted file under bin/ prints the `uncommitted changes` line once and requests nothing. (n) Request rules without a busy service: the test process itself takes `service.lock` with `LOCK_EX` and writes owner.json (its own pid, a code, `started_ok: true`), standing in for a service, then runs `fm_autopilot.py running` against the fixture: a committed new id writes `request`; an uncommitted edit under bin/ then clears it; a revert to the stand-in's code clears it; with owner.json lacking `started_ok` (or `pid: None`) a pending `request` is left untouched even when the current code equals the recorded one. `handoff_target` is unit-tested: None for a None, dirty or equal current id, the current id otherwise. (o) Outcome survives an `fm` command during start-up: in the slow-start case (k), an `ensure` run while the new serve is still inside `recover_jobs` leaves `request` in place, and the new serve then records `outcome: reloaded`, so the next ensure prints `reloaded:` once. (j) Dirty then clean: start the service with an uncommitted change under bin/ that is then committed unchanged (same tree ids as the dirty snapshot): owner.json `code` has `dirty: true`, the next ensure on the now clean tree requests a reload, and the service reloads to the clean id. (k) Slow start: a committed change whose `recover_jobs` sleeps longer than FM_AUTOPILOT_RELOAD_WAIT but less than twice it: the old service exits without recording `failed`, `failed_ids` stays empty, no `reload-failed-` wake is queued, and `outcome` ends `reloaded`. (l) `bin/fm-autopilot.sh status` prints the reload.json fields (`request`, `outcome`, `failed_ids`) in its JSON beside `running` and owner.json, after a request and after an outcome. (m) A pin in the same file: extract by name the body of `code_id` in bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py and of `board_code_id` in bin/fm-herdr.py and assert every `git` invocation in those two bodies carries `--no-optional-locks`; the rest of fm-herdr.py (for example the review-checkout `rev-parse` calls at :1401-1405) is not touched or pinned. (i) While ensure's temporary owner.json (`pid: None`, with `code`) is in place, `running` prints nothing and records no `legacy_seen`; tests (b) and (h) assert no `predates self-reload` line appears during a handoff. (d) owner.json with the `code` field removed (rewrite it while the service runs) prints the `predates self-reload` line once for that pid, writes no `request` and sends nothing to the service; owner.json with `code: null` (rewrite it likewise) gets a request for the current id and reloads. (e) Handoff failure: commit a bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py that raises at import, compute its code id with `code_id`, then have the test itself set reload.json `request` = `{to: <that id>, from: <owner code>, requested}` under start.lock and ring with `life.ring_events` (the broken `running` cannot write it): the old service records `outcome.kind: failed` for that `to` and adds it to `failed_ids`, re-executes itself from the previous snapshot (never two holders of service.lock at any moment, and at the end a live holder whose owner.json `code` and `snapshot` are the old ones), and queues exactly one `reload-failed-` wake; `bin/fm-autopilot.sh ensure` exits non-zero while the broken commit is HEAD. Then commit a working change on top: the next ensure prints the failed line once, requests the new id, and the service reloads to it. (f) A new service that dies after `ready` but before `recover_jobs` returns (commit a bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py whose `recover_jobs` begins with `raise SystemExit(70)`; fm_autopilot.py still imports, so `running` writes the request): the old service sees no holder with `started_ok` within the wait, records `failed`, and re-executes itself; reload.json `outcome` is `failed` and stays so after the re-executed old serve starts (it writes no `reloaded`). (h) Probes during handoff: while (b)'s handoff runs, a thread calls `A.live(directory)` in a tight loop; the reload still succeeds (new holder with `started_ok`, outcome `reloaded`, nothing in `failed_ids`); and a second `serve` started by hand while a service holds the lock returns 0 after about 2 s. (g) HEAD moves between request and handoff: commit A and B, then the test itself sets `request` = `{to: <A's id>, from: <owner code>}` under start.lock and rings: the handoff starts B, the old service counts that as success, `outcome` is `reloaded` with `to` = B. All waits in these tests set FM_AUTOPILOT_RELOAD_WAIT to a few seconds. (2) `reload_due` unit cases in the same file, on a Pilot whose `data` is built in the test: a job `running`, a job `consuming`, an action `started`, a non-empty batch and an unpushed wake each return false; only `uncertain`/`done` jobs, `done`/`uncertain` actions and pushed wakes return true; a `to` recorded as `failed` returns false; a `to` equal to own code returns false. (3) Board notice cases in tests/session.test.sh beside its board_start cases (:150-240), in a new git fixture of their own (a temporary root `git init`-ed with board/ and i18n/ committed), while `self.repo` and the `reused_board` helper (:219-234) stay non-git and unchanged: a fresh start records `code`; two `board_start` calls in a row with no change keep `code` and write no `stale`; after a commit under board/ the next call reuses the board (no process started or signalled; patch `os.kill` and the start to assert neither is called), keeps the old `code`, and returns `stale: true` with both `stale_reason` lines; after reverting that commit the next call writes neither field; a dirty board/, no board.json, a board.json without `code`, and a non-git root each write no `stale`. A `fm board` case asserts the two `fm board:` lines on stderr and exit 0. Existing callers that stay green unchanged: tests/autopilot-lifecycle.test.sh (its fixture root is not a git work tree, so code is None and nothing reloads), tests/autopilot-entrypoints.test.sh (stubs fm-autopilot.sh and fm_autopilot.py), tests/settings.test.sh:52-62 (no board.json: reuse, `board_matches` called once), tests/session.test.sh:380, :469 and :492-526 (non-git fixtures: code None, reuse, one child), tests/herdr/lifecycle.py, tests/decide.test.sh, tests/gate.test.sh, tests/preflight-lifecycle.test.sh, tests/option-loop.test.sh (fm-autopilot.sh gains no flag).

Docs, edited in place (T-189: nothing appended at the end of design.md): design/design.md §15.8 'Pilot and advanced integration', the paragraph beginning 'The T-141 resident service starts through `fm-session.sh start`' (about :5274-5285): the service records its code identity; `ensure` requests a reload when the engine checkout's committed bin/ or skills/ differ; the service drains (no running or consuming job, no started action, batches flushed, wakes pushed) and its old code hands off to a fresh ensure and falls back to itself if the new code does not come up, queuing one wake when the handoff itself fails; it is never killed; a dirty tree keeps the old code; the outcome is printed on the next `fm` command; a service started by `fm-session.sh start` runs the session's frozen copy, taken from the engine checkout moments earlier; while the committed code cannot import, `fm` commands report the autopilot unavailable and the old service keeps serving; a service started before T-203 is restarted by hand once. design/design.md §11, subsection 'Managed session defaults' (:2717), the paragraph beginning 'Board reuse is verified' (:2742): a verified board whose recorded board/ and i18n/ tree ids differ from the checkout's is reused but reported stale, in English and Chinese, with the instruction to restart it by hand; automatic replacement is a separate follow-up. docs/autopilot.md first paragraph (:3-13): the same reload sentence. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, the `bin/fm-autopilot.sh ensure --all` bullet (about :226): one sentence that a merged autopilot change reloads itself after its running jobs, so firstmate never kills the service. bin/fm.sh `board` usage text (about :106-110): one sentence that `fm board` says, in English and Chinese, when the board runs older code and must be restarted by hand.

In flight and ordering. Nothing in state.json is migrated or rewritten; reload.json is a new file, and owner.json and board.json gain fields. T-204 (restack ledger removal) has merged (base 6c9d1ba); every bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py line cited here is against that base. T-203 edits only `live`, `ensure`, `serve`, `main` and new module-level helpers in that file, and leaves the `Pilot` class body, the migration block (:66-108, including `migrated_t204`) and every restack, recheck, advance and launch-review function alone. No other open task edits bin/fm-autopilot.sh, bin/fm-herdr.py's board functions or design §15.8's lifecycle paragraph. Automatic board replacement is left for a separate follow-up task; board/server.ts is not touched.
